tip.title: Claim, evidence, reasoning
tip.text: A CLAIM is what someone says is true. EVIDENCE is the proof: facts, numbers, quotations, examples, expert findings. REASONING explains how the evidence supports the claim. Strong evidence is specific, relevant, and checkable. Weak support is just opinion, exaggeration, or a story about one person. When a question asks which sentence best supports an idea, pick the one that directly proves it, not just mentions it.

passage.title: Should Classes Start Later?
passage.text:
Most public high schools in the country start classes at 6:00 or 7:00 in the morning. A growing number of teachers, doctors, and students are asking whether this is wise.

The case for a later start rests on sleep science. Research on adolescents shows that during the teenage years the body's internal clock shifts: teenagers naturally fall asleep later and wake later than children or adults. A 2019 review of studies covering more than 300,000 students found that those who started school later slept an average of 40 minutes more per night and reported less daytime sleepiness. In one Philippine survey of Grade 7 to 10 students, two out of three reported sleeping fewer than seven hours on school nights, below the eight to ten hours doctors recommend.

Lack of sleep is not a small matter. Sleep-deprived students have been shown to score lower on memory tasks, get sick more often, and have more accidents on the way to school. Several schools abroad that moved their start time to 8:30 recorded improved attendance and fewer tardy marks within a year.

Opponents raise practical concerns. Later dismissal means students travel home in heavier afternoon traffic, and parents who start work at seven would have to leave children unsupervised. Some teachers also argue that the hot afternoon hours are the worst for learning. These are real problems, but they are problems of scheduling, not of biology, and schedules can be changed.

words.meaning: young people between childhood and adulthood; teenagers
words.example: Adolescents need more sleep than adults.
The plant was deprived of water and wilted.
She got a tardy mark for arriving after the bell.

items.prompt: What is the author's main CLAIM?
choices: Teenagers are lazy.
Schools should consider starting classes later because teenagers need more sleep.
Afternoon traffic is heavy.
Doctors recommend eight hours of sleep.
items.why: The whole text builds the case for a later start; the other options are details or wrong.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the STRONGEST evidence that later starts help students sleep more?
choices: "Most public high schools... start classes at 6:00 or 7:00."
"A 2019 review of studies covering more than 300,000 students found that those who started school later slept an average of 40 minutes more per night."
"Lack of sleep is not a small matter."
"Schedules can be changed."
items.why: It is specific, large-scale, and directly measures the effect of later start times on sleep.

items.prompt: The author says sleep loss causes real harm. Which evidence supports this?
choices: Teenagers' internal clocks shift.
Sleep-deprived students score lower on memory tasks and get sick more often.
Parents start work at seven.
Two out of three students sleep fewer than seven hours.
items.why: This sentence lists the harms themselves. The others describe causes or the situation, not the harm.

items.prompt: Which of these would be the WEAKEST support for the claim?
choices: A survey of 300,000 students
A doctor's recommendation of eight to ten hours
One student saying she feels tired
Attendance records from schools that changed their start time
items.why: A single person's feeling is not strong evidence. The others are large studies, expert advice, or records.

items.prompt: How does the author respond to the opponents' concerns?
choices: By ignoring them
By admitting they are real but calling them scheduling problems that can be solved
By saying parents are wrong
By agreeing to keep the early start
items.why: "These are real problems, but they are problems of scheduling, not of biology, and schedules can be changed."

items.prompt: Which sentence shows the author's OWN opinion rather than a reported finding?
choices: "A 2019 review of studies covering more than 300,000 students found that those who started school later slept an average of 40 minutes more per night."
"Two out of three reported sleeping fewer than seven hours on school nights."
"Several schools abroad that moved their start time to 8:30 recorded improved attendance."
"These are real problems, but they are problems of scheduling, not of biology, and schedules can be changed."
items.why: Calling the concerns "problems of scheduling, not of biology" is the author's judgment. The other three sentences report what studies, surveys, and records found.

items.prompt: "Research on adolescents shows that during the teenage years the body's internal clock shifts." Who are adolescents?
choices: Doctors who study sleep
Teenagers
Parents who start work early
Young children
items.why: The same sentence says the research is about "the teenage years," so adolescents are teenagers.

items.prompt: "The body's internal clock shifts: teenagers naturally fall asleep later and wake later." What does internal clock mean here?
choices: A wristwatch worn to bed
The school's bell schedule
The body's natural timing for falling asleep and waking
An alarm clock in the bedroom
items.why: The words after the colon explain it: the clock is inside the body and controls when teenagers fall asleep and wake.

items.prompt: "Parents who start work at seven would have to leave children unsupervised." What does unsupervised mean?
choices: Without an adult watching them
Without breakfast
At school too early
Stuck in traffic
items.why: The clue is that the parents have already left for work, so the children would be home with no adult to watch them.

items.prompt: Whose point of view does the LAST paragraph mainly present before the author answers it?
choices: Sleep researchers who studied 300,000 students
People who oppose a later start, such as working parents and some teachers
Grade 7 to 10 students who sleep too little
Doctors who recommend eight to ten hours
items.why: The paragraph opens with "Opponents raise practical concerns" and lists worries about traffic, parents' work hours, and hot afternoons before the author replies.
